selectedProduct.name: Communication-access card
selectedProduct.firstUser: A person who wants to explain communication preferences in their own words
selectedProduct.firstSituation: Before or during a healthcare, school, work, service, or unfamiliar conversation
selectedProduct.firstTask: Make a short card, edit the example, choose what is visible, review exactly what will leave the device, save it locally, and export a copy
selectedProduct.reason: A working implementation and product requirements already exist. The complete task is small enough to check now, has clear user control and privacy boundaries, and can support several areas without asking the person to name a diagnosis.

comparison.name: Communication-access card
comparison.existingAlternative: Paper card or ordinary notes app
comparison.engineeringEvidence: 6/6 browser tests passed; local save/reload/delete, hidden-content exclusion, review-before-export, keyboard use, 320px layout, and no external requests are covered
comparison.mainRisk: A card cannot make another person listen; wording must be reviewed by people who would use it

comparison.name: Reading and writing desk
comparison.existingAlternative: A current reader plus text editor
comparison.implementation: Product brief only; not implemented in this slice
comparison.relativeEffort: Medium for plain text; larger for scanned documents and reliable speech
comparison.mainRisk: Text extraction, speech privacy, and source fidelity can create new errors

comparison.name: Show me the time steps
comparison.implementation: Product brief only; not implemented in this slice
comparison.mainRisk: Date, travel, rounding, and money assumptions can look certain when they are not

testMethod.mode: engineering-only; no participants or demand claim
testMethod.result: 6/6 prototype tests, 4/4 acceptance tests, and 1/1 dedicated decision-flow test passed at 320px and 1280px

observations: The privacy boundary and the two-column editor/preview relationship are clear on desktop.
The phone layout becomes one column and keeps the editor usable without horizontal scrolling.
The temporary mobile success message was visually too large over the editor; its mobile padding and text size were reduced in this slice.
visualReview.limits: This is not an independent model review, participant review, screen-reader certification, or native Android/iOS test.

nextDecisionTest.comparison: Compare the card with a person's current paper or notes method on the same fictional task.
measure: whether the person can make and change the card without unwanted assumptions
whether the person can identify exactly what will be shared
whether the card adds effort compared with the current method
whether the person would choose to use it in the named situation
changeDirectionIf: the existing method is easier and the card adds no clear control or access benefit
people do not want to show a card in the target situation
the card causes privacy or wording problems that cannot be fixed without changing its purpose
